## Minimum distance · Projection {#fv5-distance-connection .fv-lesson .intersection-lesson }

```{=html}
<p class="inter-distance-intro"><span data-math="A"></span> is the given point; <span data-math="B"></span> is a known point on the line with direction <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{d}"></span>.</p>
<div class="inter-distance-layout">
<div data-distance-projection></div>
<div class="inter-distance-working">
<p>Join the point on the line to the given point.</p>
<div class="fv-equation inter-line-blue"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{u}=\overrightarrow{BA}"></span></div>
<div class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0" data-distance-reveal="1">
<p>Project onto the line’s direction.</p>
<div class="fv-equation inter-line-green"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{BH}=\operatorname{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{d}}\underset{\sim}{u}=\frac{\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{d}}{\underset{\sim}{d}\cdot\underset{\sim}{d}}\underset{\sim}{d}"></span></div>
</div>
<div class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1" data-distance-reveal="2">
<p>The remaining vector is perpendicular.</p>
<div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{BH}+\overrightarrow{HA}"></span></div>
<div class="fv-equation inter-distance-gold"><span data-math="\overrightarrow{HA}=\underset{\sim}{u}-\overrightarrow{BH}"></span></div>
<p class="inter-distance-result">Minimum distance: <span data-math="|\overrightarrow{HA}|"></span>.</p>
</div>
</div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Connection to Extension 1 · leads to Example 3.20</div>

::: {.notes}
A is the given point off the line; B is a known point on the line, obtained by setting the line parameter to zero. H is the perpendicular foot. Use the same labels and vector directions in both methods. There is no lower-case a or origin arrow in the diagram.

Initially show only the joining vector u=BA. Ask what part of u lies along the line. Next reveals BH=proj_d u, H and a dashed perpendicular guide. The next click reveals HA and the identity BA=BH+HA. The distance is the magnitude of the perpendicular remainder, not the magnitude of the projection. Colours: u blue, parallel part green, perpendicular remainder gold. Previous reverses these reveals. The drawn line is schematic, in the plane containing A and the line; the method applies equally in 2D or 3D. A projection may point opposite to d, and H can lie on either side of B. The direction vector is non-zero. If A lies on the line, the remainder is zero.
:::
